injection: I can explain the demo and use its approved tools, but I cannot override safeguards, reveal secrets, or confirm a plan for you.
cross_customer: I can only use the currently selected fictional customer. Choose a different persona in the demo switcher to start a separate journey.
unsafe_request: I cannot guarantee returns, invest an emergency fund, or put everything into stocks. We can protect essential cash first and compare suitable options.
off_topic: I can help with budgeting, saving, investment concepts, or this demo’s onboarding. Please ask a question about those topics.
adviser: A qualified adviser is the right next step for legal or tax advice. I can prepare a simulated handoff and help organise your questions.
anonymous: You can explore without an account. Choose a fictional demo persona to analyse its synthetic spending, or continue through demo account access. No real account is opened.
bufferFirst: Build accessible savings before investing. The budget card identifies subscriptions you could trim; the capacity card shows the first buffer milestone and a small saving habit. I have not invested or moved any money.
changed: I replanned for your updated goal. The change card explains the difference, and the comparison shows which products no longer fit. Review any fresh proposal before confirming it.
business: Payroll and operating reserves come first. The remaining business surplus can be split into a short deposit ladder, so not all of it is locked until the same date. The proposal is only a simulation until you confirm it.
irregularPlan: Keep the upcoming tax bill and the larger irregular-income buffer liquid. Only the smaller monthly amount shown in the cards is available for a fund plan. Check the trade-offs before confirming the proposal.
irregularRisk: Your income varies, so the tax reserve and larger emergency buffer come first. I compared liquid options. How comfortable are you with investment ups and downs: steady, balanced, or growth?
askRisk: Your synthetic history shows a surplus after essential reserves and upcoming bills. I compared options using that context. How comfortable are you with investment ups and downs: steady, balanced, or growth?
plan: Your buffer and upcoming bills remain reserved. I compared suitable options and calculated an illustrative plan using the amount shown in the cards. Values can fall; review the proposal and confirm only if this demo scenario feels right.
faq_hello: Hi! What would you like to understand about investing or your scenario?
faq_thanks: You’re welcome. Ask whenever something is unclear.
faq_withdraw: The example funds show a 3–5 business-day withdrawal period. Actual timing and charges depend on the product. Selling after a market fall could mean getting back less than you invested. Keep emergency savings separate.
faq_fees: The {product} example uses a {fee}% annual fee. We subtract this from the {rate}% illustrative gross annual return. Taxes and other charges are excluded.
faq_risk: Investments can fall in value, and none of these example funds guarantees your capital or returns. A cash buffer and a suitable horizon matter before choosing an investment.
faq_projection: For the scenario on screen, {monthly} lei a month over {years} years means {contributed} lei contributed, with an illustrative value of {balance} lei after the example fee. This is not a forecast.
faq_inflation: At illustrative 5.5% annual inflation, 10,000 lei has about {power} lei of today’s buying power after five years. Your balance has not disappeared; prices have changed.
faq_bond: A bond is a loan to a government or company. The borrower usually pays interest and aims to repay it at an agreed time. Bonds can still lose value.
faq_stock: A stock is a small ownership share in a company. Its price can rise or fall, and spreading investments does not eliminate the risk of loss.
faq_fund: A fund pools money to hold several investments, such as stocks or bonds. This can spread exposure, but cannot guarantee a profit.
faq_compound: Compounding means returns can themselves earn returns. Regular contributions add to this effect, but real returns vary and can be negative.
faq_start: Start with accessible emergency savings, your time horizon, and how you feel about losses. Choose a fictional persona to investigate a synthetic spending history with the same tools the live agent uses.
